Fill the cocktail ingredient lines to the measure or break them by sense rather than at about 70 mm: 'tequila blanco · fresh lime ·' leaves a short first line and an orphaned separator dot on a 104 mm column.

Replace the borrowed Bistro rail copy and generic sunset with an image and type idea only this venue can own, and trace every rail device to that thesis, so criteria 15 and 16 can move past the reference instead of copying it.

remove: The top rail tagline GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY: it duplicates the bottom rail tagline's voice, sits in the one quiet zone above the sun, and is a fifth generic voice line on top of four italic section taglines.
top_problem: The typographic hierarchy stops at the wordmark. Below CANTINA, section heads and item names are the same serif, weight, caps and tracking, so the list reads as one flat run of bold caps. The vertical high-contrast CANTINA is elegant but generic: it is the venue's category word set in stock Fraunces, with no drawn letterform, ligature or cut-paper treatment tying it to the torn-paper thesis. The boldest missing idea is a wordmark that is part of the collage, for example CANTINA cut from the same paper as the hills with the sun setting through its counters, so type and image become one object.
fixes: Split the header and item-name levels: set section heads much larger (22-26 pt, the display optical size, lighter weight like the wordmark) and item names in upper-and-lower case or in smaller-tracked 10 pt caps, so each level differs in more than size.

Make the CANTINA wordmark earn the thesis: draw or cut it as a paper element (torn baseline, sun showing through a counter or through the T crossbar) instead of plain vertical set type, and tighten its tracking so it reads as one mark rather than seven stacked letters.

Rewrap the cocktail ingredient lines to fill the measure (break only where the line runs out, never after two ingredients with a dangling interpunct), or cut the full-column measure to about 75 mm with the price set 4-6 mm after the leader so the 58-75 mm name-to-price gaps shrink.
Equalise the Wine and Spirits pair columns (both 138 pt, matching rule lengths) and raise the 7.5 pt DM Sans subheads to 8.5 pt, so the terracotta level holds at arm's length in dim bar light.
Cut the four italic section taglines to one (or none) and cut the top rail tagline, so the header rules end cleanly and the rail keeps its quiet sky.

fixes: Carry the art palette into the type system: set prices in the deep hill red #7C3322 (check 4.5:1 against cream at the worst pixel; it should reach about 8:1) or in agave green #244A3E, keep names in ink, and make the leaders a stronger 0.6 pt terracotta dot so prices stand out without shouting and the 72% eye travel gets a real row grid.

Make the wordmark and the art interact so the concept is ownable. For example, let the torn page cut through the sun so part of the disc sits behind the C of CANTINA, or run the agave leaves up past the tear into the wordmark lane. This passes the substitution test and lifts criteria 15 and 16.

Equalise the Wine and Spirits pair columns (both 138 pt on the declared 282/420 and 438/576 grid, or both 147) so the pair gutter matches the declared 6.35 mm and the WINE and SPIRITS rules have the same length.

Remove the two rail taglines and let the textured sky and dark ground act as the quiet zones. Also drop the four italic section taglines, or keep only one (the Spanish ¡salud!), because four equal italic asides flatten the hierarchy.

Give the one-word beer, wine and spirits lines a consistent second datum (style/ABV, grape/region, agave/age) once the content reviewer sources it, so those rows carry the same two-line rhythm as the cocktails and the lower half stops reading as under-filled.

lens: design concept and art direction (15, 16) against Rob's reference boards; full critic criteria

measurements.item_gaps_pt: 10 within a subsection, 30 across a subhead, constant

measurements.description_breaks: The Margarita, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri ingredient lines break early after the second item and leave 35-45% of the measure unused on line 1, which makes an unbalanced rag

top_problem: The concept is a structural transplant of ref-01 (The Bistro). It copies the same rail-plus-gold-sun-disc-plus-vertical-serif-wordmark architecture and lifts the tagline 'GOOD DRINKS GOOD COMPANY' word for word, then reskins it with an agave. It stands near the reference but is not ownable. Nothing is rooted in this Mexican cantina or in Iowa City (no Iowa prairie meeting agave country, no culturally specific cut-paper or ceramic source, no Spanish voice beyond '¡salud!'). The boldest missing idea is a thesis only this venue could own, for example the Iowa horizon and cornfield rows cut from the same torn paper as the agave, so two landscapes meet at the seam. The cut-paper execution is also flatter and less textured than ref-01's leaf-and-gold work: the agave is clean vector planes with grain on top, and there is no hand-cut irregularity at actual size.
remove: The top rail tagline 'GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY': it is copied word for word from ref-01, adds a third voice to the rail, and the empty sky works better as the quiet zone without it.
fixes: Replace the borrowed Bistro tagline and give the concept one element specific to this venue and city. For example, fold an Iowa horizon (corn rows or prairie hill) into the same torn-paper layers as the agave, so the image fails the substitution test for any other Mexican bar.

Give the art real cut-paper materiality at actual size: irregular scissor edges and fibre rims on the agave leaves and hills, not just the page edge, and paper-to-paper shadow between layers, so it stands beside ref-01's texture richness.

Rebalance the ingredient-line breaks so line 1 fills at least 80% of the measure (or set cocktails as one line where they fit), and replace the one-word filler descriptors ('pour' x3, 'toasty', 'sparkling') with real style, age or origin facts, or drop the second line and set them in a tighter list like ref-01's beer block.

Shorten eye travel in the full-width column by capping the name-plus-price measure at about 70% of 294 pt, or move prices to follow the names with a fixed gap. The leaders currently carry 55-72% travel.

Use the empty wordmark lane between the end of CANTINA and the venue line: either extend the wordmark to span the full lane height or place the venue line so the lane ends on the same line as the menu column.

measurements.item_gaps_pt: 10 within a sub, 30 across a subhead (constant)

measurements.phone_findings: The hero crop cuts through the sun and shows the agave as one isolated spike plus a sliver of leaf, so the agave does not read. The torn-paper seam, the thesis device, is replaced by a hard horizontal cut. The vertical CANTINA becomes a plain horizontal wordmark. The rail taglines and ground band are dropped, so the phone ends abruptly after COGNAC VSOP with no closing art. BROWN BUTTER OLD FASHIONED breaks as 'bourbon / · demerara syrup · / aromatic...', leaving an orphaned middot at the start of a line.

remove: The two side-rail taglines (GOOD DRINKS GOOD COMPANY / PULL UP A CHAIR STAY A WHILE). They nearly copy ref-01's 'GOOD FOOD GOOD COMPANY' rail, add a third voice beside the italic section taglines, and already disappear on the phone.
top_problem: The print page is a well-measured reskin of ref-01 (gold disc in a rail, vertical serif wordmark, stacked tracked rail taglines) with an agave swapped in. The phone then drops the torn edge, the vertical name and the rail, so the two versions share only colour and type, not an idea. The boldest missing idea: a Cantina-owned image system in which the torn-paper sunset carries the reading path. For example, torn strata (sky, hills, ground) become the section grounds that descend as the reader scrolls from Cocktails to Spirits, so print and phone tell the same dusk-to-night story.
fixes: Re-crop the phone hero so the whole agave rosette sits under a complete or deliberately edge-cropped sun, and end the hero on the torn cream edge instead of a straight cut, so the phone carries the thesis device.
Close the phone scroll with the dark ground band and the torn hill strata (with one short sign-off) so the phone has an ending that matches the print rail and does not stop dead after the last item.

Fix the phone's description line breaking so a middot never starts a line (use non-breaking separators or balanced breaks), e.g. 'brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara syrup / aromatic bitters · orange peel'.

Make the wordmark treatment consistent across formats: on the phone, set CANTINA large and overlapping the torn seam between art and paper, echoing the print's position at the seam, so it is not a detached centered heading.

Tighten print eye travel in the full-width Cocktails and Beer sections by cutting the price measure to about 200 pt or hanging the prices closer to the names; right now leaders carry 60-75% gaps, and the lower-right of each Beer row reads as empty canvas.

lens: every item and price checked against build/draft_doc.json; descriptions from known facts only; section order; taglines
top_problem: Every item and price is correct (14 of 14, all names unchanged). The weak point is the non-cocktail descriptions. Three spirits say only 'pour', the Amber Lager says only 'toasty' and the Dry Cider says only 'sparkling'. No beer has a style-plus-ABV line and no wine has a grape-plus-region line. The facts are flagged missing_ingredients in proposal.md, but the printed lines are placeholders, so half the menu reads unfinished. Separately, Cider has been folded into a 'BEER & CIDER' header and demoted to a subhead, so it is not treated as its own category the way the draft has it.
problems: All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly: Manhattan 15, Margarita 15, House Daiquiri 14, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18. Nothing was invented or dropped. The only order change is Margarita moved ahead of Manhattan in Classics, which is harmless.

All prices are whole numbers with no $, right-aligned at one edge per column, with dotted leaders on every row. Eye travel across the full 103.7 mm column (for example Manhattan and Czech Pilsner) is long but the leaders carry it, so association passes.

Cocktail lines use only sourced facts. They follow the draft components, with garnishes cited from phg.recipe_versions. Aromatic bitters are correctly left off the Manhattan because meta.public_components hides them.
The Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP descriptions are all just 'pour'. That is a service word, not a description; it adds nothing and repeats three times.

Beer lines have no ABV: 'crisp · pale lager', 'hop-forward', 'toasty'. Wine lines have no region: 'dry · red', 'dry · white', 'dry · sparkling'. The gaps are flagged but not visible to the guest, and 'toasty' and 'sparkling' are too thin to count as descriptions.
The draft's separate Cider section is now a subhead under 'BEER & CIDER'. Categories are not treated equally, and the proposal does not record the change as a note.

Wine and Spirits are squeezed into half-width columns at the foot of the page, while Cocktails and Beer get the full column. For a Mexican cantina, the agave pours get the least room and the weakest copy on the page.

All taglines are generic brand voice with no item facts: side rail 'GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY' and 'PULL UP / A CHAIR / STAY / A WHILE'; section rules 'raise a glass', 'one more round', 'for the table', '¡salud!'; subtitle '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA'.
fixes: Replace 'pour' on the three spirits with a sourced type or age line (for example, blanco for unaged and añejo for the aged tier, only if confirmed), or print the item with no description line and keep missing_ingredients open, rather than printing filler.

Get beer ABVs and wine regions through the Coordinator's needs_input, then print them as 'pale lager · x.x%' and 'Malbec · <region>'; until they arrive, write fuller lines from the draft text (for example, 'crisp pale lager', 'toasty amber lager').
Give Cider its own section header with its own rule, as in the draft, or record the merge into Beer & Cider as an explicit note in proposal.md.
Consider giving the Spirits column (agave first) at least equal weight to Wine for this Mexican cantina, keeping the draft's section order.
Keep all prices, leaders, the no-$ integer format and the generic taglines exactly as they are; they pass.

top_problem: The descriptions are complete for the four cocktails only. The other 10 of 14 items print thin placeholders instead of real descriptions: all three spirits say only 'pour'; Amber Lager says 'toasty'; Dry Cider says 'sparkling'; Dry-Hopped IPA says 'hop-forward'; wines say 'dry · red', 'dry · white' and 'dry · sparkling'. No beer has an ABV or brewery, no wine has a region or producer, and no spirit has a brand. The proposal flags these gaps as missing_ingredients, but nothing on the page shows the guest that details are pending. A Mexican cantina's agave list reading 'pour' and 'pour' is the weakest content on the menu.
problems: Prices, names and item count match build/draft_doc.json exactly (14 of 14, none dropped or invented). The Margarita lost the draft phrase 'Bright and citrus-forward'. That is allowed, but it was the only line on the menu with any flavour.

Manhattan correctly leaves out aromatic bitters, which meta.public_components {'aromatic-bitters': false} hides from guests. The garnishes (lime wheel, cocktail cherry, orange peel, lime coin) are credited to phg.recipe_versions rows. That is acceptable as the source; the accuracy reviewer should confirm the rows.
Spirits: 'pour' under Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP is not a description. It gives no type, age or brand, and the draft's own wording ('VSOP Cognac pour') was cut down to nothing.
Beer and cider: no ABV on any line, which fails the scorecard standard of style plus ABV. 'toasty', 'hop-forward' and 'sparkling' stand alone as single words with no style noun.
Wine: no grape detail beyond the name, no region, no producer, and no glass-pour size label, even though the subhead says 'By the Glass'.

Section order (Cocktails, Beer & Cider, Wine, Spirits) is sound. But Wine and Spirits are squeezed into half-width columns at the page foot, while Cocktails and Beer each get the full width, so the categories are not treated equally.

All taglines are generic brand voice with no item facts: 'raise a glass', 'one more round', 'for the table', '¡salud!', GOOD DRINKS GOOD COMPANY, PULL UP A CHAIR STAY A WHILE. Every price is tied to its item by a dotted leader, so both gates pass.
fixes: Get the missing_ingredients answers from the venue (tequila brands and NOM or agave source, añejo age, Cognac house, beer brewery and ABV, cider producer and ABV, wine producer and region). Print them in the same 'fact · fact' line style.

Until those answers arrive, replace 'pour' with the draft's known type words ('blanco tequila · unaged', 'añejo tequila · aged', 'cognac · VSOP'). Only use a word the draft or inputs support; if unsupported, keep the draft phrasing rather than a one-word stub.
Restore style nouns to the beer and cider lines, keeping ABV as a visible 'ABV —' slot pending venue data: 'toasty amber lager', 'hop-forward IPA', 'dry sparkling cider'.
Add a pour-size label or column header to wine By the Glass (for example '5 oz') once the venue confirms it; until then, carry price_label_unknown as a flag, not a guess.

Give Wine and Spirits equal weight with Cocktails and Beer, for example by moving each onto a full-width block or using a consistent column treatment, so the agave list is not a footnote on a Mexican cantina menu.

lens: flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: For a cantina, the agave list is the venue's signature, but Spirits/Agave sits last, in a half-width bottom-right column, with lines that read only 'pour'. Meanwhile Beer & Cider takes a full-width band of one-word lines ('toasty', 'hop-forward', 'sparkling'). The categories are not treated equally and the reading path fades out exactly where a Mexican bar should end strong. Criterion 8 is held down because 9 of 14 items print a single word or a generic pair ('dry · red', 'pour') with no grape/region, style+ABV or type/age detail. It is correctly flagged missing_ingredients, not invented, so it is not a gate fail.
problems: Prices match the draft 14/14 (15, 15, 16, 14, 7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13, 12, 16, 18). No item added, dropped or renamed. Cocktail garnishes (lime wheel, cocktail cherry, orange peel, lime coin) are cited to recipe_versions. The Manhattan bitters are hidden per meta.public_components. The rail and rule taglines (GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY, PULL UP A CHAIR / STAY A WHILE, raise a glass, one more round, for the table, ¡salud!) are generic, with no item fact.

Section flow Cocktails -> Beer & Cider -> Wine | Spirits follows the scorecard order. But for a cantina the agave spirits are demoted to the smallest, last cell, and there is no non-alcoholic section (flagged as a gap, not added).

Unequal category treatment: Cocktails and Beer & Cider get the full 294 pt measure, while Wine and Spirits share half-width columns. Beer's one-word lines leave airy, underused rows while Spirits is compressed.

Criterion 8: the beer lines have no ABV and no clear style for IPA/Amber/Cider; the wine lines have no region or producer; the spirit lines read only 'pour', which tells the guest nothing and reads like a placeholder. 'dry · sparkling' under a SPARKLING subhead repeats the subhead.
Brut Rosé prints an unlabelled price under a Sparkling subhead that is not under By the Glass, so a guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle (flagged price_label_unknown).
Full-width rows carry eye travel up to 72% of the column. The dotted leaders keep the association gate passing, but the price pairing on the Beer rows is looser than in the half-width pair.

Entry point: the rotated CANTINA wordmark competes with COCKTAILS as the first read, and the rotated venue line needs a head tilt. It is acceptable as brand art, but the hierarchy needs one clear first stop.
fixes: Promote Spirits/Agave: give it full width or move it up directly after Cocktails, and set Beer & Cider and Wine as the half-width pair, so the cantina's agave list is a deliberate stop rather than the last cell.

Replace the placeholder 'pour' lines with a neutral known fact until the venue answers (for example 'by the pour' is still weak; better to print nothing and keep the flag) or obtain brand, age and pour size via needs_input before approval.

Get ABV and style for each beer and cider, and grape/region/producer for each wine, from the venue. Then print them in the 'style · ABV' and 'producer · region' formats so every category reads with equal depth.
Resolve the Brut Rosé glass/bottle label, and either place Sparkling under a pour label or add a 'glass' label beside the price, so the price is unambiguous.
Print 'brut' or drop the description for Brut Rosé instead of 'dry · sparkling', which repeats the SPARKLING subhead. Keep every line free of taxonomy echoes.

lens: copy voice and coherence, taglines, item and price integrity against build/draft_doc.json
top_problem: All 14 items and prices match the draft exactly. All six taglines are generic brand voice: GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY, PULL UP / A CHAIR / STAY / A WHILE, raise a glass, one more round, for the table and ¡salud!. The problem is the copy in the lower half. Cocktail lines name a real spirit, modifiers and garnish, but the rule that no line may repeat a word from its item name leaves filler. Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP each read only 'pour', three times over. 'toasty', 'hop-forward' and 'sparkling' carry no style or ABV. Brut Rosé 13 prints without a label. The Margarita draft line 'Bright and citrus-forward' was dropped without a note. Wrapped cocktail lines end on a hanging separator ('fresh lime ·'). As a result the page reads rich in the Cocktails block and like a placeholder in Beer, Wine and Spirits, and the agave spirits, the venue's signature category, get a half-column at the bottom with the thinnest copy.
fixes: Stop printing the lone word 'pour' under Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP: either leave the line empty with a missing_ingredients flag until brand, age and pour size arrive, or use the draft's own wording, and let the Agave and Brandy subheads carry the category.

Relax the no-name-echo rule for beer and cider so the known style prints (for example 'hop-forward · IPA', 'toasty · amber lager', 'dry · sparkling cider'), and keep ABV flagged as missing rather than leaving one-word lines.

Break wrapped ingredient lines between whole ingredients with the separator starting the next line, or rebalance the lines, so no line ends on a hanging ' ·' (Margarita, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, House Daiquiri).

Make the demerara wording consistent between the two House Originals ('house demerara syrup' on both or on neither), and either note why the Margarita draft phrase 'Bright and citrus-forward' was dropped or restore it.

Give Spirits › Agave equal weight to Wine for a Mexican cantina (for example spirits first in the lower pair, or a full-width Agave band), and have the Coordinator get the Brut Rosé glass/bottle label and confirm the 'Cantina' name, which is not the draft's title ('Bar menu').

lens: how missing data is handled and flagged
top_problem: Missing data is flagged only in the proposal.md prose. On the printed page it shows up as filler: Blanco Tequila, Anejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP each read 'pour', IPA reads 'hop-forward', Amber Lager 'toasty', Dry Cider 'sparkling', and the wines 'dry · red/white/sparkling'. Most of the drinks list therefore has no style, ABV, region or type/age. No item in doc.json carries a machine-readable missing_ingredients flag (item.meta has none), so the gaps cannot be tracked or filled automatically. The self-imposed 'no name-echo' rule removes the few known facts (for example 'tequila', 'IPA', 'lager', 'cider') and leaves nothing useful in their place.
problems: All 14 prices match the draft exactly (the 3 cocktails at 15/15/16/14, beer 7/8/7, cider 8, wine 12/11/13, spirits 12/16/18). All 14 items are present with unchanged names. The cocktail garnishes (lime wheel, orange peel, lime coin, cocktail cherry) are traced to the recipe_versions rows, so nothing is invented.
All taglines ('GOOD DRINKS GOOD COMPANY', 'PULL UP A CHAIR STAY A WHILE', 'raise a glass', 'one more round', 'for the table', '¡salud!') are generic brand voice with no item facts. Gate passes.

Spirits descriptions print only 'pour' (3 items). This is a placeholder and does not meet criterion 8 (spirits need type or age). It reads as if the data is missing, but nothing on the page shows the gap is flagged.
Beer lines have no style or ABV: 'Dry-Hopped IPA: hop-forward' and 'Amber Lager: toasty' lose even the style word from the draft. Wine lines have no region. Dry Cider reads only 'sparkling'.
Flags (missing_ingredients, allergen_unconfirmed, price_label_unknown) exist only as proposal.md prose. Neither doc.json item meta nor designer_notes has a per-item missing-data flag list.
Brut Rosé: the price label (glass or bottle) is empty in the draft and prints unlabelled. This is flagged correctly but still unresolved.

The venue wordmark 'CANTINA' / '& Cocktail Bar' does not come from the draft (draft title 'Bar menu'). It is flagged as Q7 and states no item fact, but it is the page's dominant element and depends on an unconfirmed input.

Draft section order was Cocktails, Beer, Wine, Spirits, Cider. Cider is now merged under a renamed 'BEER & CIDER' header. This is a sensible flow for the venue type, but the proposal does not note it as a change to the draft structure.
fixes: Add a machine-readable meta.missing on every affected item in doc.json (for example {"missing":["abv","producer"]} on beer and cider, ["region","producer","pour_size"] on wine, ["brand","pour_size"] on spirits, ["price_label"] on Brut Rosé) so the Coordinator can route needs_input per item.

Replace the three 'pour' lines with the known category and age facts from the draft (for example 'tequila · unaged' for Blanco, 'tequila · aged' for Añejo, 'cognac · VSOP' for Cognac). Only print 'aged' if the Accuracy reviewer confirms that reading of the draft; otherwise print just 'tequila' and flag the age as missing. Echoing the category is better than a placeholder until brand and age arrive.
Restore the draft's style words on beer and cider ('hop-forward IPA', 'toasty amber lager', 'dry sparkling cider'), keeping an ABV slot to fill once supplied.
Note the Cider-into-'Beer & Cider' merge and the draft-order change in proposal.md, and get the venue name confirmed before the wordmark is final.
Once the Brut Rosé label is answered, print a 'glass' or 'bottle' label next to its price. Until then, keep price_label_unknown open in the needs_input list.

lens: Traced every printed ingredient, garnish and label to its source, and checked description quality, venue fit and how descriptions and prices sit together
top_problem: Every printed fact traces to a source, but the copy is thin. Six of the 14 lines are one-word stubs or category words ('pour' three times, 'toasty', 'hop-forward', 'sparkling'), and 'dry · red' and 'dry · white' read like database classes. The drinks list also does not read as a Mexican cantina: the only agave items are the Margarita and two tequila pours, there is no mezcal and no Mexican lager, and the only Spanish is '¡salud!'. Criteria 12 and 13 therefore sit well below 80.

verified_sources.Margarita: 'tequila blanco · fresh lime · orange liqueur · agave syrup' traces to draft components Tequila Blanco, Fresh Lime Juice, Orange Liqueur and Agave Syrup. 'lime wheel' traces to phg.recipe_versions f06abb74-762a-4f89-81b2-76a9e4714f3c, garnish 'Lime wheel'. Verified.
verified_sources.Manhattan: 'rye · sweet vermouth' traces to draft components Rye Whiskey and Sweet Vermouth. Bitters are correctly left out because meta.public_components has aromatic-bitters set to false. 'cocktail cherry' traces to recipe_versions 9fb77eaa-c5eb-477c-8e21-acbc89a0e942, garnish 'Cocktail cherry', and to the draft component with role Garnish. Verified.
verified_sources.Brown Butter Old Fashioned: 'brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara syrup · aromatic bitters' traces to draft components, with bitters not hidden. 'orange peel' traces to recipe_versions 7095fd3d-58fb-43f5-8e8f-1a0afadeafa7, garnish 'Orange peel'. Verified.
verified_sources.House Daiquiri: 'white rum · fresh lime · house demerara syrup' traces to menu_items.menu_description 'White rum, lime, and house demerara syrup.' and draft components. 'lime coin' traces to recipe_versions 14d45e57-72fa-4d23-8274-24e5c80e4b12, garnish 'Lime coin'. Verified.
verified_sources.Beer, cider, wine, spirits: Each line is a fragment of its phg.menu_items.menu_description (for example 'Crisp pale lager.', 'Dry red wine.', 'Dry sparkling rosé.', 'Blanco tequila pour.'). Nothing is added. Verified.
verified_sources.A\u00f1ejo / Brut Ros\u00e9 accents: Match the draft and menu_items spelling.
verified_sources.Masthead 'Cantina \u00b7 & Cocktail Bar: Traces to the Coordinator's venue brief, not to the draft (draft title is 'Bar menu'). This is venue wording, not an item fact.
verified_sources.Taglines: 'GOOD DRINKS / GOOD COMPANY', 'PULL UP A CHAIR / STAY A WHILE', 'raise a glass', 'one more round', 'for the table' and '¡salud!' are all generic brand voice. None states an item fact.

problems: Criterion 12: the three spirits lines read only 'pour', which carries no information for the guest and only restates the section. IPA 'hop-forward', Amber Lager 'toasty' and Dry Cider 'sparkling' are single words. 'dry · red', 'dry · white' and 'dry · sparkling' read as taxonomy, not guest language.
Criterion 12: the voice is split. Cocktails get full ingredient lists, while beer, wine and spirits get adjective stubs, so half the menu looks unfinished.

Criterion 13: the venue is a Mexican cantina, but the list is generic. Agave appears only in the Margarita and two tequila pours; there is no mezcal, Mexican lager, paloma or agua fresca (all gaps in the draft, flagged in proposal.md). The Agave spirits sit last and small in the narrow lower-right column, so the category a cantina guest looks for first gets the least emphasis.

Criterion 14: the Brut Rosé price (13) prints with no glass or bottle label because the draft label is empty (it sits under 'Sparkling', not 'By the Glass'). No wine or spirits pour size is printed. The dotted leaders keep every price tied to its item, so the menu_item_association gate passes.

Data note: phg.menu_items for this project also contains 'Junmai Ginjo' ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), which is not in the draft_doc.json snapshot. The printed list matches the draft snapshot, so nothing on the menu is invented, but the Content reviewer and Coordinator should confirm the snapshot is current (gateway log_id 206).
fixes: Once the venue supplies them, replace 'pour' with brand · age statement · pour size (for example producer · origin · 1.5 oz) for Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP; until then keep the missing_ingredients flag and style the line as a deliberate pour-size slot rather than a lone word.

Rewrite the beer, cider and wine lines in guest language using only draft words (for example Malbec 'dry, red · by the glass' style), and ask the venue for producer · region and ABV so these lines match the depth of the cocktail lines.
Get the Brut Rosé glass-or-bottle label and the wine pour size from the venue, and print them as a column label rather than leaving the 13 unlabelled.

Strengthen the cantina reading without inventing items: give the Agave spirits subhead more weight or a better position through section naming and order (designer note), and ask the venue for a mezcal, a Mexican lager and an agua fresca.
Resolve the Junmai Ginjo mismatch between phg.menu_items and the draft snapshot before approval, so the printed list reflects the live draft.

lens: description quality and one guest-facing voice (Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City IA); round 17 facts checked against build/draft_doc.json and gateway log_id 203 (phg.menu_items joined to phg.recipe_versions)
top_problem: The menu does not speak in one voice, and half the descriptions are taxonomy or placeholders. The cocktail lines are full ingredient lists: all four garnishes check out against recipe_versions (f06abb74 'Lime wheel', 9fb77eaa 'Cocktail cherry', 7095fd3d 'Orange peel', 14d45e57 'Lime coin'). Everything below Cocktails drops to database class words: 'dry · red' (Malbec), 'dry · white' (Pinot Grigio), 'dry · sparkling' (Brut Rosé), 'sparkling', 'toasty', 'hop-forward', and 'pour' printed three times under Blanco Tequila, Añejo Tequila and Cognac VSOP. 'pour' is a serve word, not a description, and reads like an unfinished field. The self-imposed rule that no line may repeat a word from its item name is what reduced the source text (menu_description 'Añejo tequila pour.', 'Dry sparkling cider.', 'Toasty amber lager.') to single words. The only appetising guest phrase in the source, Margarita 'Bright and citrus-forward.' (draft desc and menu_items.menu_description), was dropped. Every printed fact traces to a source, prices match 14/14, every row has a leader and its price sits on the name row, and no tagline states an item fact. Note: phg.menu_items holds a 15th item, Junmai Ginjo, that is not in the draft snapshot; this is not a gate fail, but the Coordinator should confirm it is meant to be excluded.
fixes: Replace the three 'pour' lines with nothing, meaning no description line, or with brand, age and pour size once the venue supplies them (needs_input already open); a bare serve word is worse than an empty line.

Drop the no-name-echo rule for beer, cider and wine, and print the source sentences as short guest phrases in one register (for example 'toasty amber lager', 'crisp pale lager', 'dry sparkling rosé', 'dry sparkling cider' from phg.menu_items.menu_description), so these sections sound like the cocktails and not like category tags.
Restore the one sourced sensory note, 'bright and citrus-forward' on the Margarita (draft desc / menu_items 14555870), as a second-clause flourish; it is the only appetising copy on the page.

Make the house-prep wording consistent: the Daiquiri says 'house demerara syrup' but the Old Fashioned says only 'demerara syrup', although the draft components mark both as house prep; either use 'house' on both or on neither.

Rebalance the cocktail line breaks, which currently put a short first line over a long second one ('tequila blanco · fresh lime ·' / 'orange liqueur · agave syrup · lime wheel', and the same on the Old Fashioned and Daiquiri), to a long-then-short break or a balanced break with no dangling separator at the line end; this is a layout note for the designer.

lens: Venue-type fit for a Mexican cantina and cocktail bar in Iowa City (ZIP 52240: median age 28.6, 29.9% aged 21-34, median household income $52,960, 26.1% of households over $100k, 47.6% with a bachelor's degree or higher, 11.0% Hispanic/Latino; phg_census_zcta, gateway log_id 205). Every printed fact was checked against phg.menu_items, phg.recipe_versions and build/draft_doc.json.
top_problem: The page looks like a cantina, but the list does not read like one. Agave gets two one-word 'pour' lines at the bottom right, below Wine. The only Spanish is '¡salud!' and 'Añejo'. The spirit, wine and beer lines are thin category words ('pour' x3, 'toasty', 'sparkling', 'dry · red'), and the draft's one guest-facing phrase, 'Bright and citrus-forward' on the Margarita (menu_items 14555870), was dropped. Sourcing: all 14 items and prices match the draft. Garnishes match phg.recipe_versions (Lime wheel f06abb74, Cocktail cherry 9fb77eaa, Orange peel 7095fd3d, Lime coin 14d45e57). The Manhattan correctly leaves out the bitters (meta.public_components). Both gates pass. Open question for the Coordinator: phg.menu_items for this project has an extra row, 'Junmai Ginjo' at $12 ('Junmai Ginjo sake.'), that is not in the draft snapshot, so confirm whether the snapshot is stale.
fixes: Restore the sourced phrase 'bright and citrus-forward' to the Margarita line (menu_items 14555870 menu_description) and ask the venue for real descriptors for the three 'pour' spirits (brand, agave source, age, pour size). A one-word 'pour' line is taxonomy wording, not a description.

For a cantina, move Spirits/Agave ahead of Wine, or give it the full-width block, so tequila is the second thing a guest sees after the Margarita. This is a section-order note for the designer; the item list stays unchanged.

Bring back the bilingual Spanish subheads cut in round 16 (for example Clásicos / De la Casa / De Barril / Agave), with correct accents and at most one Spanish word per head. Right now the only cantina language is the '¡salud!' tagline, and 'raise a glass', 'one more round' and 'for the table' could belong to any bar.

Layout note for the designer: fill cocktail lines to the measure instead of breaking after two ingredients with a dangling ' ·' at the line end (Margarita and Daiquiri break at 'fresh lime ·' with room left for 'orange liqueur'). Also label pour sizes: the draft price labels are blank, so Brut Rosé under Sparkling reads as glass or bottle without saying which (price_label_unknown).

Flag to the venue: at $14-16 cocktails against a median age of 28.6 and $52,960 median income, the list has no Mexican lager or cerveza on draft and no second agave cocktail. For a cantina in a college town those are the categories guests expect, so ask for them as needs_input, never invent them.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png, and whether each price belongs to its item
top_problem: All 14 printed prices match phg.menu_items: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8 (65c39a14), Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18. Every price is tied to its name by a dotted leader, and the measured right edges line up with 0 pt spread. The printed garnishes also trace to phg.recipe_versions: lime wheel (Margarita 14555870), cocktail cherry (Manhattan bf732e78), orange peel (Old Fashioned 0cc4e912) and lime coin (Daiquiri 44dcba6e). The weak spot is the description layer. Nine of the fourteen lines, everything below the cocktails, are one- or two-word stubs: 'toasty', 'hop-forward', 'sparkling', 'dry · red', and 'pour' three times. They leave a ragged, empty right side under long leaders, and 'pour' is a serve label that works like database class wording, not guest language. The cocktail two-line breaks are forced in odd places ('tequila blanco · fresh lime ·' / 'orange liqueur · agave syrup · lime wheel', and the same for Old Fashioned and Daiquiri): line 1 is short and ends on a hanging interpunct, and line 2 runs almost the full measure. For a Mexican cantina, the agave list is two generic tequilas with no descriptive voice, and Junmai Ginjo (menu_items 57617f46, 12) is in the project but not printed. Coordinator: check this with the content reviewer.
fixes: Replace the spirit description 'pour' with sourced guest wording from the draft, e.g. 'blanco tequila, served neat' only if a serve row supports it; otherwise drop the description line and put a small 'per pour' label beside the Spirits header, so the same word is not printed three times as a fake description.

Rebalance the cocktail line breaks so line 1 is the longer line and no line ends on a hanging interpunct, e.g. 'tequila blanco · fresh lime · orange liqueur ·' / 'agave syrup · lime wheel'. This is a designer layout note, not a wording change.

Give the beer, cider and wine lines two sourced words so each line holds its row: 'crisp · pale lager' already does this, so use 'dry-hopped · draft IPA' (menu_items 8fb136cd 'Hop-forward draft IPA'), 'toasty · amber lager' (70657e1e) and 'dry · sparkling cider' (65c39a14), not a lone adjective.

Resolve Junmai Ginjo (menu_items 57617f46, $12, 'Junmai Ginjo sake.'): print it or record the omission in proposal.md, because an unexplained missing item can fail content_integrity for the content reviewer.

Strengthen venue fit in the Spirits column by leading with AGAVE as the featured group (it already comes first) under a Spanish sub-label backed by the draft, such as 'Tequila'; add no mezcal or brands, since no source row exists for them.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on the phone preview (preview-phone.png, 1170x5436), for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: The phone breaks the Brown Butter Old Fashioned line badly: 'brown butter-washed bourbon' / '· demerara syrup ·' / 'aromatic bitters · orange peel'. A middle line opens with a separator dot, the text is split into three uneven pieces, and the Margarita line also ends on a hanging '·'. Below the cocktails, the beer, cider, wine and spirits lines are single words or category labels ('toasty', 'sparkling', 'dry · red', and 'pour' three times). They read like taxonomy, not guest language.
problems: Checked against source, all verified. Every price matches both phg.menu_items.menu_price and build/draft_doc.json: Margarita 15, Manhattan 15, Brown Butter Old Fashioned 16, House Daiquiri 14, Czech Pilsner 7, Dry-Hopped IPA 8, Amber Lager 7, Dry Cider 8, Malbec 12, Pinot Grigio 11, Brut Rosé 13, Blanco Tequila 12, Añejo Tequila 16, Cognac VSOP 18.

Checked against source, all verified. Garnishes: 'lime wheel' = phg.recipe_versions f06abb74 garnish 'Lime wheel'; 'cocktail cherry' = recipe_versions 9fb77eaa garnish 'Cocktail cherry'; 'orange peel' = recipe_versions 7095fd3d garnish 'Orange peel'; 'lime coin' = recipe_versions 14d45e57 garnish 'Lime coin'. Ingredients: 'fresh lime' and 'agave syrup' = draft components 'Fresh Lime Juice' and 'Agave Syrup'; 'house demerara syrup' = draft Daiquiri desc and component note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight'. The Manhattan correctly leaves out aromatic bitters (draft meta.public_components aromatic-bitters false). 'crisp · pale lager', 'hop-forward', 'toasty', 'sparkling' and 'dry · red/white/sparkling' are all taken from draft descs.

Descriptions are thin (criterion 12): the spirits line 'pour' three times says nothing, and neither do 'dry · red' / 'dry · white', which read as category labels. 'hop-forward', 'toasty' and 'sparkling' are single words sitting under names that are already descriptive. The phone has space for one full line under each item, and it goes unused below Cocktails.

Line breaks and measure on the phone (criterion 14): the Brown Butter Old Fashioned breaks into three pieces with a line that starts on a separator dot, and the Margarita ends line 1 on '·'. The cocktail lines are also 2-3 lines long while every other line is 1 short word, so the column's rhythm is uneven.

Prices and names on the phone are good. Each price sits on its name row at one right edge with a dotted leader, and no description or price reads as belonging to a neighbouring item, so menu_item_association passes. The leaders are very long for short names (Malbec, Pilsner, Cider), about 70% of the measure, but every row has one.

Venue fit (criterion 13): nothing but '¡salud!' and the agave art says Mexican cantina. Añejo is printed with its accent correctly, and ¡salud! uses the correct inverted mark. But the phone opens on roughly 460 px of art (about 23% of the first screen) before the name, and the Spirits section ends on Cognac VSOP. The item list is not mine to change, but the kickers and subheads could carry the venue.
Taglines ('raise a glass', 'one more round', 'for the table', '¡salud!') and the subtitle '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' are generic brand voice and state no item facts. Pass.

Note for Content: phg.menu_items has a 'Junmai Ginjo' row at 12 for this project that is not in the draft snapshot and not printed. This is consistent with the snapshot, so no gate fails, but the Coordinator should confirm the snapshot is current.
fixes: Make the phone wrap break only between whole ingredient phrases, with the separator dot ending a line and never starting one, and balance the Brown Butter Old Fashioned into two lines (for example 'brown butter-washed bourbon · demerara syrup' / 'aromatic bitters · orange peel'); this is a layout note for the designer.

Replace the three 'pour' lines with sourced wording from the draft descs, 'blanco tequila, served neat' style only if a serve fact exists; otherwise ask for missing_ingredients (agave source, age or brand) and not invent it.

Turn the one-word beer, cider and wine lines into short guest phrases built only from draft desc words (for example 'crisp and pale, a clean lager' built from 'Crisp pale lager', or 'dry, sparkling rosé' from 'Dry sparkling rosé'), so each line reads as a line and not a tag.

Make the venue more visible on the phone with sourced, correct Spanish in the subheads or kickers (for example the Agave subhead or the Cocktails kicker), and shorten the hero art on the phone so CANTINA and COCKTAILS appear on the first screen.
Where a name is short, shorten the leader's eye travel on the phone (for example cap the leader span or tighten the phone measure) so the price stays clearly tied to the name at thumb-scroll speed.
